title: Given an integer array, return an array where each position holds the product of all other elements, without using division and in linear time.
shortTitle: Product of Array Except Self: Prefix Product Times Suffix Product
keyPoints: The except-self product at each index is the prefix product (everything left) times the suffix product (everything right).
A left-to-right pass fills the result array with prefix products; a right-to-left pass multiplies in suffix products.
No division is used, so zeros are handled naturally without any branching.
The result array holds prefix intermediates during the first pass; the only extra variable is a suffix scalar, giving O(1) extra space.
O(n) time with exactly two linear passes through the array.
Use BigDecimal for financial growth factors to keep products exact and avoid overflow.
This is the same precompute-and-combine approach as prefix sums, applied to multiplication.

s1_definition.oneliner: Fill each slot with the product of everything on its left, then multiply in the product of everything on its right.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Product of Array Except Self** – for each index, compute the product of all other elements without division, in O(n) time.
- **Prefix product pass** – left-to-right: `result[i]` = product of all elements before index i.
- **Suffix product pass** – right-to-left: multiply each `result[i]` by the product of all elements after index i.
- **O(n) time, O(1) extra space** – the result array stores intermediates; one suffix scalar is the only extra variable.
- **Zero-safe** – zeros are handled naturally with no special branches.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India has a row of daily growth factors for Rajesh's portfolio and wants, for each day, the combined growth of all the other days. Instead of dividing the total by that day, which breaks if any day is zero, the clerk makes one left-to-right pass writing the running product of earlier days, then one right-to-left pass multiplying in the running product of later days.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│    Product of Array Except Self: Two Passes              │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                          │
│  Array:  [ a0,  a1,  a2,  a3 ]                           │
│                                                          │
│  Pass 1 (→ prefix):                                      │
│  result: [  1, a0, a0*a1, a0*a1*a2 ]                     │
│                                                          │
│  Pass 2 (← suffix):                                      │
│  suffix starts at 1, multiplied in right-to-left         │
│  result: [a1*a2*a3, a0*a2*a3, a0*a1*a3, a0*a1*a2]       │
│                                                          │
│  Each slot = prefix * suffix = product of all others     │
│  Extra space: 1 suffix variable = O(1)                   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Product of Array Except Self asks for, at each position, the product of every other element, without division and in linear time. The two-pass approach fills each slot with the prefix product (everything to its left) in a left-to-right sweep, then multiplies in the suffix product (everything to its right) in a right-to-left sweep. Each position ends up with the product of all elements except itself.

The result array stores prefix intermediates during the first pass, and the only extra variable is a single suffix scalar, so extra space is O(1) beyond the output. Division is avoided entirely, which means zeros are handled for free: one zero makes every other position zero, two or more zeros make everything zero, all without branching.

For financial growth factors, use BigDecimal with multiply to keep products exact. This is the multiplication analog of prefix sums, using the same precompute-and-combine structure.

In a banking project at the National Bank of India, this computes the combined growth contributed by all days except each individual day, useful for leave-one-out sensitivity analysis on Rajesh's portfolio.

Remember one sentence: Sweep left for prefix products, sweep right multiplying in suffix products, and each position holds the product of everything except itself, with no division and O(1) extra space.
